subject: Post-call: BrightCart scale qualification & autoscale action items
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@brightcart.com>, Priya Suresh <priya@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: BrightCart scale qualification & autoscale action items

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we all have the same frame for the SLO/scale conversation. I focused on the performance and autoscale topics you flagged: latency targets, concurrency/throughput expectations, streaming behavior, and how warm pools/queueing should behave during spikes.

Summary of BrightCart targets (as described on call):
- Traffic profile: multiple spikes during promotions; peak concurrent sessions ~3k user sessions, peak request concurrency for the inference endpoint ~600 concurrent requests (short bursts up to 1,200 for <10 minutes).
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end response latency <= 350ms for non-streaming generation (1–2k token outputs). For streaming scenarios, first token RTT p95 <= 120ms and steady-state per-token latency additive <= 10ms/token.
- Throughput: sustained token throughput target ~1.2M tokens/min during peak windows.
- Availability / graceful degradation: prefer fast fallback to a smaller quantized variant for 5–10% of requests under heavy overload, preserving core UX.

Key autoscale expectations discussed:
- Warm pool target: keep ~40 pre-warmed workers during expected promotional windows (configurable by schedule).
- Scale-up: cold-to-ready (able to accept requests without extra queueing) for a single additional worker within ~18–30s; bulk scale from 40 -> 160 within ~120s under aggressive autoscale policy.
- Queueing behavior: prefer bounded request queue with FIFO, backpressure signal returned to client at ~500ms queue wait; Redwood to provide metrics and suggested client retry/backoff.

Action items (owners and dates):
1) Rishi: deliver detailed SLA matrix and measurement plan (attached spreadsheet) by Mon 2026-04-05.
2) Marissa: propose runbook for promotional warm-pool scheduling + escalation path by Tue 2026-04-06.
3) BrightCart (Evan): confirm acceptable fallback model(s) and which endpoints can tolerate quantized outputs by Mon 2026-04-05.
4) Aditya: propose an initial load-test plan and sample test harness (JMeter script + perf runner) by Wed 2026-04-07.

Notes on measurement: we'll use p95 over 5-minute rolling windows for acceptance and will instrument both token-level latencies (runtime) and end-to-end (service + network). Streaming latencies will be measured at first-byte and then per-token inter-arrival. We'll share dashboards and raw traces for the first load run.

Attachments: burst-sla-matrix.xlsx (SLA table + baselined numbers), observability-checklist.pdf (suggested metrics & tracing spans).

Next step: Evan, if you can confirm the fallback tolerance and sign off on the Monday items, we'll schedule the first load run the following week (target window Thu 2026-04-15).

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Park <evan.park@brightcart.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya@brightcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightCart scale qualification & autoscale action items

Thanks Rishi — useful recap. A couple of clarifying q's before we sign off on the plan: 
1) When you say "bulk scale 40 -> 160 in ~120s", is that optimistic or measured on Redwood's dedicated tier? We need both warm-pool behavior and the worst-case cold provisioning times for Dedicated vs Hosted.
2) For the streaming first-byte p95 <= 120ms, is that measured from our client (AP east coast) to first byte or Redwood's regional edge? We need to know whether client network variance is included.
3) On fallback model: our product team can accept a smaller quantized variant for lower-quality suggestions in the cart flow but not for checkout or fraud detection endpoints. We'll list endpoints in the matrix.

We'll confirm the endpoint tolerances by EOD Monday. One more ask: can you include an example queue-backpressure response payload so our frontend can implement the correct UX?

—Evan
Sr. Platform Engineer, BrightCart

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@brightcart.com>, Priya Suresh <priya@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightCart scale qualification & autoscale action items

Evan — thanks, answers inline: 
1) The 40->160 in ~120s figure is for our Dedicated offering with burst autoscale policy and accelerated pool provisioning; it's based on observed runs across similar customers but we'll validate during the load run and mark it as a target in the SLA matrix (sheet: provisioning_assumptions). For Hosted (shared) the worst-case cold provisioning could be longer — we flag that in the spreadsheet and recommend Dedicated for your promotional windows.
2) Streaming first-byte p95 <= 120ms is measured edge-to-client (so it includes network). We'll provide both server-side first-byte and edge-to-client measurements in the dashboard so you can separate network variance.
3) Great — please mark checkout/fraud endpoints as NO-FALLBACK in the matrix and we'll treat them as hard SLOs.

Queue-backpressure payload (example):
{
  "error": "request_queued",
  "queued_position": 42,
  "estimated_wait_ms": 480,
  "retry_after_ms": 600
}

We'll attach this example in the observability checklist and include recommended client backoff behavior (exponential with jitter, cap at 5s).

Action update: I attached an updated SLA matrix (same filename) with notes on Dedicated vs Hosted provisioning. Marissa will send the runbook tomorrow and Aditya will send the initial load test scaffolding. After your final endpoint list we'll schedule the load window; Thu 2026-04-15 still looks good from our side.

-Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@brightcart.com>, Priya Suresh <priya@brightcart.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightCart scale qualification & autoscale action items

Thanks — looping in a couple quick operational notes from our side: 
- Runbook draft link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/brightcart-scale-docs (folder contains escalation tree, run commands, and warm-pool schedule template).
- For the promo windows we recommend a scheduled warm-pool ramp starting T-1h with an initial pre-warm of 40 workers and an incremental policy (40 -> 80 at T-45m -> 120 at T-20m). This cadence minimizes queueing during ramp and keeps cost predictable.
- Observability: we'll provision a shared dashboard for you with token-level latencies, p95/p99 traces, queue depth, worker health, and model-variant ratio. We will also expose a Kafka topic with raw event logs for your analytics team if you want deeper ingestion.

Confirmed items: BrightCart to send endpoint tolerances today; Redwood to share SLA matrix and queue-backpressure payload (done), runbook draft (in folder), and Aditya will post the load-test harness by Wed.

Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
